result:
Full `go vet ./...` and `go build ./...` are clean across the whole module. The fix is complete and not pushed, per instructions.

Summary of the change:

- **`internal/state/state.go`**: `RemoveProject` now runs entirely in one transaction. It checks agent count, deletes every project-owned table (new `projectOwned` var: `agent_seq`, `pr_watches`, `agent_queue`, `agent_events`, `checkpoints`, `questions`, `notifications`, `running_turns`, `chat_items`, `chats`, `secrets`, `connectors`, `connector_projects`, `skill_projects`, and the project-memory tables `memory_serves`, `memory_anchors`, `memory_duplicates`, `consolidation_passes`, `working_memory`, `memories`, `agent_reports`, `artifacts`, `events`), deletes the project row, and renumbers — fixing the `agent_seq` foreign-key crash and the stale rows left behind for projects added again under the same name. A new `projectKept` map documents the three tables intentionally left alone (`agents`, `media`, `token_usage`) and why. The old separate `RemoveProjectConnectors`/`RemoveProjectSecrets`/skill_projects calls (each its own non-transactional statement) are folded into the one transaction; those two helper methods stay, since other tests call them directly.
- **`internal/state/sections.go`**: removed `renumberProjects`, now dead code since its only caller runs `renumber` inline on its own tx.
- **`internal/state/removeproject_test.go`** (new): one test builds two projects each with an agent, secrets, a chat and media, destroys the agent, removes one project, and checks every `projectOwned` table is clear, the other project is untouched, media survives, and agent numbering restarts at `agent-01` after re-adding the project. A second test walks live `sqlite_master`/`pragma_table_info`/`pragma_foreign_key_list` and fails if any table with a `project` column or FK to `projects` is missing from both `projectOwned` and `projectKept` — verified it actually catches an omission by temporarily removing `notifications` from the list and confirming the test failed, then restored it.

`go test ./internal/state` and `go vet ./internal/state` (and `go vet ./...` / `go build ./...`) all pass. Nothing pushed, per the task.
